title: Uncovering co-regulatory modules and gene regulatory networks in the heart through machine learning-based analysis of large-scale epigenomic data.
authors: Vahab, Naima; Bonu, Tarun; Kuhlmann, Levin; Ramialison, Mirana; Tyagi, Sonika
one_liner_zh: 该文用CNN和随机森林基于大规模ChIP-Seq表观数据预测转录因子共结合模块并映射基因调控网络，虽聚焦TF共结合而非直接TF-DNA三维互作建模，但方法可迁移至TF-DNA结合位点预测研究。
abstract: The availability of large-scale epigenomic data from various cell types and conditions has yielded valuable insights for evaluating and learning features predicting the co-binding of transcription factors (TF). However, prior attempts to develop models predicting motif co-occurrence lacked scalability for globally analyzing any motif combination or making cross-species predictions. Moreover, mapping co-regulatory modules (CRM) to gene regulatory networks (GRN) is crucial for understanding underlying function. Currently, no comprehensive pipeline exists for large-scale, rapid, and accurate CRM and GRN identification. In this study, we analyzed and evaluated different TF binding characteristics facilitating biologically significant co-binding to identify all potential clusters of co-binding TFs. We curated the UniBind database, containing ChIP-Seq data from over 1983 samples and 232 TFs, and implemented two machine learning models to predict CRMs and the potential regulatory networks they operate on. Two machine learning models, Convolution Neural Networks (CNN) and Random Forest Classifier(RFC), used to predict co-binding between TFs, were compared using precision-recall Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curves. CNN outperformed RFC (AUC 0.94 vs. 0.88) and achieved higher F1 scores (0.938 vs. 0.872). The CRMs generated by the clustering algorithm were validated against ChipAtlas and MCOT, revealing additional motifs forming CRMs. We predicted 200k CRMs for 50k+ human genes, validated against recent CRM prediction methods with 100% overlap. Further, we narrowed our focus to study heart-related regulatory motifs, filtering the generated CRMs to report 1784 Cardiac CRMs containing at least four cardiac TFs. Identified cardiac CRMs revealed potential novel regulators like ARID3A and RXRB for SCAD, including known TFs like PPARG for F11R. Our findings highlight the importance of the NKX family of transcription factors in cardiac development and provide potential targets for further investigation in cardiac disease.
abstract_zh: 来自不同细胞类型和条件下的大规模表观基因组数据的可用性，为评估和学习预测转录因子（TF）共结合的 features 提供了宝贵见解。然而，先前开发预测基序共现模型的尝试缺乏可扩展性，无法全局分析任意基序组合或进行跨物种预测。此外，将共调控模块（CRM）映射到基因调控网络（GRN）对于理解潜在功能至关重要。目前，尚无全面的流程用于大规模、快速且准确的 CRM 和 GRN 识别。在本研究中，我们分析并评估了促进生物学显著共结合的不同 TF 结合特征，以识别所有潜在的共结合 TF 簇。我们整理了 UniBind 数据库，包含来自超过 1983 个样本和 232 个 TF 的 ChIP-Seq 数据，并实施了两种机器学习模型来预测 CRM 及其作用的潜在调控网络。两种机器学习模型，卷积神经网络（CNN）和随机森林分类器（RFC），用于预测 TF 间的共结合，通过精确率-召回率受试者工作特征（ROC）曲线进行比较。CNN 优于 RFC（AUC 0.94 对比 0.88），并实现了更高的 F1 分数（0.938 对比 0.872）。通过聚类算法生成的 CRM 与 ChipAtlas 和 MCOT 进行了验证，揭示了形成 CRM 的额外基序。我们预测了 50k+ 人类基因的 200k 个 CRM，并与最近的 CRM 预测方法进行了验证，重叠率为 100%。此外，我们缩小了研究范围，专注于心脏相关调控基序，过滤生成的 CRM 以报告 1784 个包含至少四种心脏 TF 的心脏 CRM。识别出的心脏 CRM 揭示了潜在的新型调控因子，如 ARID3A 和 RXRB 与 SCAD 相关，包括已知的 TF 如 PPARG 与 F11R 相关。我们的发现强调了 NKX 转录因子家族在心脏发育中的重要性，并为心脏疾病的进一步研究提供了潜在靶点。
